Where ΔH is the enthalpy change of the reaction and T is the absolute temperature in kelvin.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Dissolving an ionic solid is always an exothermic process.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
At equilibrium, moving towards either pure reactants or pure products would decrease total entropy (making ΔS<sub>total</sub> negative). Only the equilibrium mixture gives maximum total entropy.

front_blocks.md: Is the decomposition of CaCO<sub>3</sub> spontaneous at **293 K** given ΔH = +177.9 kJ mol<sup>-1</sup> and ΔS<sub>sys</sub> = +160.4 J K<sup>-1</sup> mol<sup>-1</sup>?

back_blocks.md: ΔS<sub>surr</sub> = −177900 / 293 = −607.2 J K<sup>-1</sup> mol<sup>-1</sup>
ΔS<sub>total</sub> = +160.4 + (−607.2) = −446.8 J K<sup>-1</sup> mol<sup>-1</sup>
ΔS<sub>total</sub> is **negative**, so the reaction is **not spontaneous** at 293 K.
